title: TLS 1.3 Handshake
description: A Mermaid sequence diagram of the 1-RTT TLS 1.3 handshake between client and server, with notes explaining ephemeral Diffie-Hellman, the point where traffic becomes encrypted, CertificateVerify, AEAD application data, and forward secrecy.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Trace the TLS 1.3 handshake message by message and name what each defends against.
Explain how ephemeral DH provides forward secrecy.
Identify where the connection transitions from plaintext to encrypted.

instructionalStrategies: Read top to bottom, pausing at each note to name the defensive purpose of the step.
Compare the 1-RTT flow with the TLS 1.2 summary to motivate why fewer options is more secure.

assessmentQuestions.question: What does CertificateVerify prove, and why is it necessary in addition to sending the certificate?
An attacker records a TLS 1.3 session and later steals the server's long-term key. Can they decrypt the recording? Why or why not?

chapter_title: "Cryptography in Practice: PKI, TLS, and Data Protection"
